premise: Larry begins, "This is how the show is made," and the camera stops listening and goes into his mouth to see for itself. Each place it reaches is the making of the place before, and the way down is always through whatever is doing the talking. It ends when the head it is trying to enter is forty-two pixels across.
turn: The bottom is a profile picture
screen: LEVEL 0, the desk: Larry starts the sentence. The camera pushes between his lips. LEVEL 1, inside the head: the vocal tract as a cave in glowing lines, the jaw a drawbridge, the tongue a moving floor, the lips the gate behind us, the velum a curtain. Larry, voice over: every voice is synthesized from this model, and the heads move exactly as the engine's did. The owner's post crediting the synth and the head model hangs here as a card. The line being said passes through as a ribbon, and the camera follows it back. LEVEL 2: the ribbon flattens into a cue file, a long hall of tick marks, one per word, each with its start and end. Pictures hang off the ticks. At each cue a flash goes off: a frame is shot and looked at. LEVEL 3, the far end of the hall: the fitting room. The same line is said over and over to a line-drawn ear that writes down what it heard. "Kazoo" comes out "clue". "Repost" comes out "report". A sound-editor puppet respells. LEVEL 4, behind the ear: the writers' room. A writer puppet types "This is how the show is made." One door carries the hook's own description of itself: "a guard, not a wall". LEVEL 5, the page on the writer's desk: under the brief is the fact sheet (written by the project manager, checked line by line by an auditor), and under that the commission. The camera goes into the commission's word "recursive". LEVEL 6, inside the word: a desk and a head, opening its mouth to say the sentence. The camera goes for the mouth and bounces off: the head is a circle 42 pixels across, the size the profile picture was judged at. A pink dot on its ring is flicked away. Larry, voice over: "That is the bottom. You cannot go into a profile picture." Button, a very small Larry: "Forty-two pixels."
format: an explainer as one continuous push-in
notes: EXPLAINS: what the show is made of (the vocal-tract heads, offline audio, cue files, frames shot at every cue), fitting, who writes, and how this script came to exist. RECURSIVE: levels 4 to 6 are the making of the explanation (the writer, the fact sheet, the commission), and level 6 is the whole thing starting again. ENDS: at the profile picture, because a 42-pixel head has no mouth to go into; Larry says so. THREE DIMENSIONS: every level is a place, and the picture moves by going through a mouth, along a line, through an ear, into a page. Only the four parts the sheet names are drawn in the head. The mishearings are two of the listed harmless ones, word and what was heard, with no source. The pink dot was on one candidate picture and was removed: it is said as that. Puppets in process roles are house puppets, never a model speaking.

premise: On Larry's desk there is a scale model of the studio, and he uses it to explain how the show is made. On the model's desk there is a smaller model, which explains how that explanation was made. An auditor stands in each doorway and lets the camera through only if there is a record of what is inside.
turn: It stops for lack of paperwork
screen: LEVEL 1, the model on the desk: the camera drops into it like a helicopter shot. Thirteen rooms round a courtyard, one per stage, each holding the files it writes. In the courtyard a line-drawn machine with no head carries folders from room to room: the tool that calls no model. Numbers from the last full run are painted over the doors as the camera passes: 73 cards, 38 kept, 548 ideas, 9 drafts, 6 selected. LEVEL 2, the model on the draft room's desk: an auditor puppet checks a clipboard and waves the camera in. This model is the commission: seven rooms. Three are solid (the owner asks; the project manager writes the fact sheet; an auditor checks every line and makes a card). The fourth is being drawn as we arrive: identical booths with no windows between them, a writer puppet in each, each holding the same little model and not knowing it. Rooms five to seven are dotted outlines with signs in the future tense. LEVEL 3, the model in room two: the auditor waves us in again. The making of the fact sheet: one page the size of a floor. An auditor strikes out lines; a project-manager puppet writes some back in from a saved log, in the log's own words. One of the lines coming back: "The first kazoo looked like a submarine; I redrew it." LEVEL 4, the model on that desk: the auditor's hand goes up. There is a desk. There is nothing on it: the sheet says nothing about how the log was made. Sibyl: "It ends at the first thing nobody wrote down." The camera hovers, then backs out through all three models to Larry. Button, the auditor: "Not on the sheet."
format: an explainer as a set of nested models
notes: EXPLAINS: the thirteen stages and what each is for, the tool that runs them, the funnel of numbers, the roles, and the rule that whoever makes a thing does not judge it. RECURSIVE: level 2 is the making of this script (the sheet's seven steps, with the script's own place in them), level 3 is the making of the fact sheet, level 4 would be the making of the log. ENDS: at the first level with no record. The auditor removed whatever the records did not support, so the stopping rule is the sheet's own. THREE DIMENSIONS: each level is a physical model on a desk inside the last, entered from above. The booths are the brainstorm stage this idea is being written in. The numbers are from an unaired draft and are said as "the last full run". The auditor is a house puppet in a role. The last level claims only that the sheet is silent on how the log was made, which is true of the sheet; it must not become a claim about what the repository does or does not hold.

premise: One tracking shot down a corridor of thirteen doors, the stages of the show. Behind the seventh a writer is drafting this script, and on the page is a shorter corridor. Each making-of is shorter than the thing it makes: thirteen rooms, then seven, then three, then one.
screen: LEVEL 1: a corridor seen side-on like a doll's house, thirteen doors, a number over each. The camera tracks along it while Larry names the stages at speed, and Eppy keeps the count on a scoreboard: 13. The funnel is painted along the skirting: 20,825 posts, 73 cards, 548 ideas, 6 segments. At door seven the camera turns in. A writer puppet at a desk; on the page, a drawing of a corridor. The camera pushes into the paper. LEVEL 2: the same corridor, smaller and paler, seven doors: the steps of this commission. Scoreboard: 7. The camera stops at door six, which is open, with the same writer inside. Door seven is only painted on the wall. Through the page in door two. LEVEL 3: three doors: the fact sheet was written, checked line by line, and had lines put back from the log. Scoreboard: 3. Through the first door. LEVEL 4: one room. Scoreboard: 1. No page with a corridor on it. On the wall, the commission's own sentence, and the owner's credit post as a card, read by Sibyl with his name. The only light in the room is a single line-drawn desk lamp, pointing. Eppy: "Thirteen, seven, three, one. It has run out of rooms." He changes the scoreboard to 0 and nothing happens. Button, Larry: "Light direction."
format: an explainer as a tracking shot with a countdown
notes: EXPLAINS: the thirteen stages in order, the funnel of numbers, and that the owner sets direction and watches before anything is published. RECURSIVE: each corridor is the making of the page found in the one before, and the levels are real (the thirteen stages; the seven steps of this commission; the making of the fact sheet; the commission). ENDS: at the commission, because each level has fewer rooms than the last and the count runs out at one room with no page in it. THREE DIMENSIONS: corridors nested through sheets of paper, each travelled along and then entered. The "three" is my reading of the sheet's opening and its last section, not a numbered list: 13, 7, 1 works without it. The owner is a card read aloud ("light direction by me"), so no ruling is needed; a puppet of him saying the credit line unprompted, as he posted it, would be his call at review. The lamp is the show's pun on his phrase and gives him no words. "High" in his post is not understood (the card says so): shown, not explained.

premise: Begin on one still frame and pull back. Every pull-back shows who was looking at the last picture and what they were checking for, so the show is explained as a chain of watchers, each in a room behind the last. Then the whole chain is pulled back from again, because this segment will be watched the same way. It ends at the inside of the glass.
screen: LEVEL 0: full frame, a line-drawn pen writing a line and stopping one letter short. Pull back through the frame's edge. LEVEL 1: it is one of a strip of stills, one a second, in front of a cold-viewer puppet who is shown frames and nothing else. Its note, read by Sibyl: a subtitle that "runs off the right edge". Pull back through the wall. LEVEL 2: that room is a picture on a reviewer puppet's desk, beside a scorecard: sixteen gates, thirteen scored rows, 21 of 26, two lines circled. Pull back. LEVEL 3: a staging review, a puppet going through frames one at a time; a counter on the wall, TOOL CALLS, reads 492. Pull back. LEVEL 4: a builder puppet, whose code the pictures are. On the bench, a kazoo that looks like a submarine, crossed out, and a second kazoo. Pull back further than the builder. LEVEL 5: all four rooms together are themselves a strip of stills in front of a second cold viewer. This is the making of the making-of: the sheet says that if this is selected, a cold viewer will be shown stills of it. The nested picture really does run off the right edge now. Pull back. LEVEL 6: a chair, headphones on a desk, nobody drawn: the owner watches it with sound. Pull back once more and the camera stops against something flat: the frame of a browser window, seen from inside. Sibyl: "It ends at the glass. Whoever is past that is not ours to draw." Button, Larry, a dot in the middle of it all: "Is it off the edge?"
format: an explainer as one continuous pull-out
notes: EXPLAINS: staging checked by shooting frames, the cold viewer, the scorecard, the staging review, pictures as code, the owner's watch before publishing, and that the show runs in a browser. RECURSIVE: the second pull-out watches the first chain of watchers, which is the real last step of this commission; a third would watch that. ENDS: at the browser's edge, because the camera cannot leave the page; the only watcher beyond it is the person watching, of whom the show has no record. THREE DIMENSIONS: every level is a room that contains the previous room as a picture, and is left through its back wall. The pen is exactly what the sheet says and nothing of what it wrote. 21 of 26, the 492 and the kazoo are from the last full run and its log, an unaired draft. The owner is not drawn and says nothing. The ending faces the viewer: a reviewer should weigh it against the anti-pattern of the audience as the punchline; here it is the end of a chain, not a joke about viewers' habits.

premise: The show has a tool that hears what the audience will hear, and it does not always hear the script. So the making of the show is explained once, and then the camera goes through the ear: each level down is the level above, rebuilt from what was heard. It stops at a word the voice has never managed to say.
screen: LEVEL 1, a clean studio: Larry explains fitting. A tool renders every line, transcribes it and looks for a spelling the voice can say; a sound editor settles what it cannot. In shot: a kazoo on the desk (the first drawing of it, the one that looked like a submarine), a sign reading NEW, a tray marked REPOST. On the desk, a line-drawn ear. The camera goes into it. LEVEL 2, the same studio as heard: the kazoo is now a clue, drawn as a magnifying glass; the tray reads REPORT; the sign reads NO, and Sibyl notes that this one would have reversed a real person's answer. Into the ear again. LEVEL 3, how that explanation was fitted: a row of Larrys, fourteen to sixteen of them, each saying the same line with a different spelling on his chyron. Eppy: a third of the Fable tokens went on drafting, and half of drafting was this. The owner's ruling comes down as a notice, and the row folds into one small machine with a crank. Into the ear again. LEVEL 4: the band. The bass is two semitones flat and the whole room sits two steps lower than it should; a writer puppet is quietly writing his notes sharp. A builder raises the floor. Into the ear again. LEVEL 5: an empty room and one word on a stand: "caterwauling". The ear on the far wall gives back the same two words every time. The camera goes in and comes out in the same room. And again. Sibyl: "It ends at the word that always comes back the same." Button, Larry: "Ted Walling."
format: an explainer as a game of whispers
notes: EXPLAINS: offline audio, the transcription check, respelling, the render-and-listen loop and what it used, the owner's ruling that made it a tool, the flat bass and its fix. RECURSIVE: each level is the making of the explanation above it, by the step the sheet gives for this very script (a tool will render every line and report what it heard). ENDS: at a fixed point, the one word never heard as itself in any spelling; going through the ear again changes nothing, and that is shown twice. THREE DIMENSIONS: the same studio rebuilt at each level, entered through the ear. Only the four harmless mishearings the sheet names are used, as the word and what was heard, never whose post, never more of it; the two the sheet does not describe are not guessed at. No spellings are invented for the walls. "Ted Walling" could be somebody's name: it stays in quotation marks as heard words (the sheet's "Ted Walling") and is never drawn as a person. The punch depends on the engine saying it clearly, which is its own risk.

premise: The show has a rule against repeating itself, kept by two reviewers who have read everything it has aired. A recursive making-of is the show repeating itself one size smaller. So the explanation goes down a level at a time until it reaches the repetition gate, and the gate does its job.
turn: The show's own rule stops it
screen: LEVEL 1: the process as a building cut in half. Top floor, the writers' room, with no stairs down. Basement, the archive of everything aired (shelves, nothing legible), and two reviewer puppets with the only key. Sibyl explains who may read what. A writer puppet tries the basement door and a line-drawn hook swings across it, tagged "a guard, not a wall". The camera, not being a writer, sinks through the floor. LEVEL 2, in the basement: on the newest shelf, one folder: this commission, a folder inside the repository whose process it describes. Inside it, the same cut-away building, smaller: writers in sealed booths brainstorming this script without seeing each other's, reviewers below about to check it against everything the show has done. Down through its floor. LEVEL 3: the building again, smaller, and upside down. Sibyl, from the ceiling: at most one item an episode may turn an old one on its head. This is the one. Down, which is now up. LEVEL 4: a turnstile and the two reviewer puppets. Beyond it a fourth building is fully drawn and waiting. One reviewer shrugs. The other shakes its head. Caption: THE STRICTER VERDICT STANDS. The turnstile does not turn. Sibyl: "It ends at the gate. The next level would be a repeat." A slip of paper is handed back and rises through every level to Larry's desk, the only thing that crosses. He reads the one line to himself. Button, Larry: "One line. Fair."
format: an explainer as a descent through a cut-away building
notes: EXPLAINS: writers never read what the show has done and reviewers do; the hook; two independent reviewers and a tool combining them; the repetition gate, where the stricter verdict stands; the single inversion an episode is allowed; the one line that goes back to a writer. RECURSIVE: level 2 is this commission inside the repository it describes, level 3 is the same again, inverted once as the rule allows. ENDS: at the repetition gate, because the next level down is a repeat by construction; how is the stricter of two verdicts, and one line comes back. THREE DIMENSIONS: the same building nested in its own basement, entered through the floor, with one level flipped by rolling the camera. Using the gate to end the recursion is the show's staging and must look like it: the script cannot claim reviewers really blocked anything, because that step has not happened when the script is written. The archive shows nothing of any episode. I cannot know what the show has already done; that is the premise, and it is the reviewers' to check.

premise: Every level of explanation has to be paid for in attention, and the show has a unit for that. The camera corkscrews down a stairwell, one level of making-of per landing, with a meter on the wall, until five reviewers stop at the same moment.
screen: LANDING 1: the roles as house puppets with signs, grouped by the model family each runs on, as the sheet lists them; the owner's credit post on the wall as a card. Larry explains who does what. The camera spirals down the stairs. LANDING 2: the last full run in numbers, one painted on each stair: 20,825 posts, 73 cards, 548 ideas, 9 drafts, 6 selected, 504.5 seconds. A meter on the wall, EFFECTIVE TOKENS, stands at about 115 million. Beside it a stopwatch: the video rendered in 157 seconds. Down. LANDING 3, the making of the making-of: the measuring itself. A pie with a third cut out (drafting) and half of that slice shaded (one loop). The owner's ruling on the wall. Then the seven steps of this commission as seven stairs, the meter still ticking on the sentence being said. Down. LANDING 4, the making of that: five reviewer puppets in a row, judging the explanation of the explanation. Mid-word all five stop, mouths open at the same shape. The stairwell lights go out from the top, one landing at a time. A long silence. Larry, in the dark: "It ends here. Usage limit." LANDING 5, in the dark below: the sound of a crank. The tool that calls no model goes on down the stairs alone, combining scores by arithmetic. The lights come back and the five finish the word. Button, Sibyl: "They were resumed and finished."
format: an explainer as a descent with a running meter
notes: EXPLAINS: the roles and the model family each runs on, the last run's numbers, effective tokens as the sheet defines them, where they went, the owner's ruling on what Fable is for, and the tool that runs the stages without a model. RECURSIVE: landing 3 is the measuring and the commission that followed it, landing 4 is the judging of this script, and the crank carries on to levels nobody watches. ENDS: on landing four, for the puppets; how is the usage limit, an incident from the last run's log placed here as staging. Below that it is arithmetic, and the show leaves it to the tool. THREE DIMENSIONS: a stairwell the camera descends in a spiral, each landing a small set. Tokens are never turned into money. Nothing is said about what a model thinks, wants or feels: the five are house puppets in a role, and they simply stop. The script must not claim the limit was hit while making this segment. The last line is the sheet's own sentence.

premise: The show is made out of the community's posts, and the post announcing the show is one of them. So the scrape that feeds the show brought back posts about the show, and this segment is made from those. The camera follows that loop round until it reaches the edge of the window.
turn: It ends on an open question
screen: LEVEL 1: up through the studio roof. The studio is one lit point in a cloud of them: 20,825 posts from 2,786 accounts, 248 of them brighter. A beam sweeps across like a lighthouse: the scraper, ordinary code, no model tokens. Where it passes, points turn into card skeletons, filled by address so no post is retyped. The camera picks a point and flies in. LEVEL 2: the owner's launch post, the card it was, 13 November, text only. Behind it his thread as a short gallery: the credit line, the source post inviting people to make their own episode, and nate's thank-you, each read aloud by Sibyl. The camera goes through the link in the source post. LEVEL 3: the repository as a building of thirteen rooms, and in one room a folder: this commission. On its table, the card this segment is made from. Painted on the wall: 202 posts about the show in the window, 9 on the card. One of the nine is the launch post. The camera flies into it again. LEVEL 4: the same gallery, six days later. bisks' card. The owner's two questions as cards, read by Sibyl with his name. bisks' puppet gives his two suggestions as the replies they were. The camera looks for the next card. There is not one. The beam stops against a wall of glass etched with a date and a time: the end of the window. Points beyond it, and no cards. Larry: "It ends where the scrape ends, on a question." Button, Sibyl: "Window's closed."
format: an explainer as a loop, with a performed exchange at the end
notes: EXPLAINS: scope and the scrape, cards filled by address, the thirteen stages, the open source and its credit, and how this card was made from posts about the show. RECURSIVE: the show is made from posts, the posts include posts about the show, the card about making the show is made from those, and the segment shows that card. ENDS: at the edge of the scrape window, on the owner's question: the show is only made of what is inside the window, and nothing on the card records an answer. THREE DIMENSIONS: a cloud of points, a gallery inside one point, a building inside a link, the gallery again inside a card. The script must not say or imply that the owner decided anything, took a suggestion or replied, that the show sends direct messages, or that a producer bot exists. bisks' suggestions are performed only as replies to the owner's follow-up, read just before them. nate's post is read aloud, never voiced, and nothing about his work is said. The launch post's video is not used. "ChimeraTV" and "talking my beat" are not understood: the posts are shown whole and not explained, or the second suggestion is dropped. The owner is cards only; a puppet would be his call.
